sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
The path was a step change rather than a cycle: revenue grew 14.3% in FY2018, 6.9% in FY2023, then 15.7% and 17.8% in FY2024 and FY2026 [D46][D311][D364][D472].
FY2026 revenue rose $50.1 billion, or 18%, driven by Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud led by Azure and Productivity and Business Processes by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud [P17].
FY2018 net income fell 35.0% on a 54.6% effective tax rate, which the filing attributes to the net charge from enactment of the TCJA [D48][D32][P61].
Microsoft Cloud supplied 16.2pp of FY2026's 17.8% revenue growth and reached 64.6% of revenue [D568][D472][D566].
Server products and cloud services revenue rose 31% to $129.4 billion, driven by Azure and other cloud services growing 41% [S61][D641][P12].
Intelligent Cloud contributed 11.2pp of FY2026 growth against 6.8pp from Productivity and Business Processes and -0.2pp from More Personal Computing [D917][D892][D942].
Operating income grew 20.8% against revenue growth of 17.8%, an incremental margin of 53.3% [D473][D472][D498].
Operating costs grew 10.3pp slower than revenue, at 7.4% [D499][D491].
Operating margin reached 46.8% in FY2026, a window high against a 41.7% median and a 30.1% low in FY2017 [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin of 67.9% sat below its 68.2% median and 69.8% FY2024 high, down 0.9pp on cost of revenue [F30][D981][D980][D486].
The FY2026 gross-margin decline came from Intelligent Cloud, where gross margin percentage fell on AI infrastructure investment and sales mix shift to Azure [P11].
In FY2026 net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below the 46.8% operating margin, as other income of $10.7 billion partly offset a 19.4% tax rate [F70][F50][X124][D458].
Operating cash flow of $182.9 billion was 1.37x net income, in line with the 1.33x FY2019 level [F100][D459][D86].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion, only 0.50x net income against a 0.91x window median, and its 20.2% margin was the window low [F120][D478][D460][D990][D456][D982].
Capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion, 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A, as investing cash use rose on a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions [F110][D479][D455][D461][P1].
Operating cash flow rose $46.8 billion to $182.9 billion on higher cash received from customers and lower income tax payments [P1].
Net cash of $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, ranks in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion [D464][D495][D463][D494].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion absorbed 72.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted count fell 0.2% [X147][X157][D468][D493].
The current ratio of 1.23x is the window low, but the net cash cushion and $76.8 billion of cash and short-term investments leave liquidity ample [F200][D991][D465][P2].
Free cash flow ran below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x [R1][D406][D460].
The gap is capex-led rather than earnings-led, so the flag matters as a signal on how long the AI buildout suppresses distributable cash [D460][D455].

FY2017 pretax income, income tax and receivables were later restated to $29.9 billion, $4.4 billion and $22.4 billion from the first-reported $23.1 billion, $1.9 billion and $19.8 billion [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
The FY2017 tax and margin comparisons rest on first-reported values, so the FY2018 tax spike should be read as directionally, not precisely, comparable [R3][D32].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the 30.3% window median from 20.2% in FY2026, reported in the FY2027 10-K cash flow statement [D984][D456].
Whether capex stays above the 34.9% of revenue reached in FY2026 or falls back toward the 22.9% FY2025 level, disclosed in the FY2027 10-K investing section [D455][D401].
Whether operating margin holds above the 41.7% window median after the 46.8% FY2026 high, shown in the FY2027 10-K segment discussion [D975][F50].
